new_statements.quote: The {Gáná orthography also employs four tone diacritics, i.e. [ ´ ] for the high tone, [ ¯ ] for the mid tone, [ ` ] for the low tone, and [ ˆ ] for the falling tone, one of which is added to a vowel or nasal letter to mark its tone.

In: Sekere, Gakedumele; Kato, Kanji; Ono, Hitomi; Nakagawa, Hirosi, ガナ語資料：モダリティ / Gǁana data: modality, Journal of the Institute of Language Research (Tokyo University of Foreign Studies) 28: 41, pp. 9-11. doi:10.15026/0002000407 (CC-BY).
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (11 pp., text layer). Page 9, 'Appendix: An outline of the Gǁana orthography (Hirosi Nakagawa)', §1 'ǁGáná alphabet': the quoted sentence is there word for word ('The ǁGáná orthography also employs four tone diacritics, i.e. [ ´ ] for the high tone, [ ¯ ] for the mid tone, [ ` ] for the low tone, and [ ˆ ] for the falling tone, one of which is added to a vowel or nasal letter to mark its tone.'); the text layer renders the lateral click letter ǁ as '{', which is the only difference from the report's rendering. The rest of the appendix (pp. 9-10) covers click/non-click graphemes and vowels; nothing on stress, accent or prominence. Intro p. 1 (Japanese) says morphemes without specified…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Gǁana is a lexical-tone language: every vowel/syllabic nasal carries one of high, mid, low or falling tone, and tone alternations are lexical/morphological (e.g. transitivity pairs khóán vs khôān, Sekere et al. 2026: 2). No Gǁana-specific source opened says anything about word stress or accent. The closest first-hand prosodic-prominence statement in the cluster is for the mutually intelligible sister language Gǀui (Nakagawa 2006 PhD, §2.2.2.3 p. 42): the bimoraic lexical root (tonal domain DOM1, three tones/six melodies) is 'always pronounced with certain auditory prominence (relatively wide pitch range, loudness and length)' which grammatical non-roots (DOM2, two tones) lack, i.e. prominence is a property of the word-initial root, not a positional stress rule.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: Loanwords and morphemes with unspecified tone are written without tone marks (Sekere et al. 2023: 1). In Gǀui (Nakagawa 2006: 42) the reduplicative copy and the third mora of trimoraic roots fall in the non-prominent domain DOM2.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns orthographic tone marking of the Gǁana Gyom dialect (New Xade) as used in fully tone-marked elicited sentences; it is an orthography note inside a data paper, not a prosody chapter. The Gǀui root-prominence statement (Nakagawa 2006) is about citation forms and is said to attenuate in running speech (Ch.2 p.~95).
new_statements.identity_note: Quoted statement is for Gǁana proper (gana1274), Gyom dialect as spoken in New Xade (Ghanzi District), per Sekere et al. The fuller prosodic description (root prominence + two tonal domains) is for the sister language Gǀui (gwii1239, Nakagawa 2006), which the author describes as mutually intelligible with Gǁana and as forming the Gǀui-Gǁana subgroup; Glottolog also files the Gǀui works under gana1274's bibliography. Nakagawa 2013 (Routledge) is headed 'ǁGana' as Vossen's subgroup label and may use Gǀui as the representative variety.

sources.note: SISTER LANGUAGE Gǀui (gwii1239; author: mutually intelligible with Gǁana, Ch.1 p.13). Word 'stress' never used. Tone: two tonological domains; DOM1 = bimoraic (lexical) root with three tones /H M L/ giving six melodies; DOM2 = non-roots (grammatical morphemes, 3rd mora of trimoraic roots, reduplicative copy) with two tones. §2.2.2.3 p. 42: 'Another prosodic property is what I call here "prominence", which is involved in DOM1. sources.note: Nothing on stress. Orthography appendix (p. 9): Gǁana orthography marks four tones (high, mid, low, falling) on vowels/nasals; all data are fully tone-marked. Establishes Gǁana as a lexical-tone language; silent on stress/accent.
